item.text: {"facts":[{"source_id":"SRC-abf6ab8d70083bde","start_unit":1,"end_unit":2,"fact_summary":"CIEP reported that Mexico’s 2023 public-education spending was projected at 3.24% of GDP, below pre-pandemic levels and the IDB’s 4.0–6.0% recommendation; it also said the allocation remained inequitable, with basic-education spending more progressive but higher-education and postgraduate spending benefiting richer households disproportionately.","question_ids":["5B.1","5B.6","5B.8","5B.10","6B.2","6B.3","6B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The source analyzes the 2023 budget projection and 2020 distributional evidence; it is relevant to López Obrador’s 2023 policy trajectory but does not establish full-year 2023 execution.","ruler_attribution":"The report evaluates the federal education budget approved or proposed during López Obrador’s administration.","limitations":["The source is an analytical report, not a complete audit of 2023 outcomes."]},{"source_id":"SRC-abf6ab8d70083bde","start_unit":4,"end_unit":5,"fact_summary":"CIEP found that public spending on early-childhood education was insufficient, private early-childhood spending was concentrated among high-income households, and the 2023 budget did not change the inequitable pattern; it warned that unequal investment amplifies developmental and opportunity gaps.","question_ids":["5B.6","5B.8","6B.2","6B.3","6B.8","6B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The report explicitly discusses the 2023 education budget while relying partly on 2020 expenditure data.","ruler_attribution":"The finding concerns federal education-budget choices under López Obrador’s government.","limitations":["It does not identify the president’s personal role in each allocation decision."]},{"source_id":"SRC-e84ad84eb6f1975e","start_unit":16,"end_unit":18,"fact_summary":"Reuters reported that López Obrador revealed a Banxico rate increase before its official announcement, later apologized, and publicly urged the bank to avoid raising rates; officials and analysts nevertheless said Banxico continued acting independently, including unanimous rate increases despite presidential pressure.","question_ids":["5B.2","5B.3","5B.7","7B.1","7B.8"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The article is from 2022 and provides institutional context carried into the 2023 assessment period.","ruler_attribution":"The reported pressure, premature disclosure, apology, and public recommendations are attributed directly to López Obrador.","limitations":["The article does not document 2023 monetary-policy decisions."]},{"source_id":"SRC-a56749c2c8afadc2","start_unit":4,"end_unit":6,"fact_summary":"The Maya Train was presented as a southeast-development and tourism project, but reporting documented forest clearing, route changes, cost overruns, delays, construction over fragile cave and aquifer systems, construction beginning before the required environmental-impact study, judicial suspension followed by a national-security decree allowing work to continue, and a later rapid environmental approval questioned by critics.","question_ids":["5B.1","5B.4","5B.6","5B.7","5B.9","6B.2","6B.6","6B.10","8B.1","8B.2","8B.3","8B.5","8B.6","8B.7","8B.8","8B.9","8B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The article, published January 2023, describes project implementation and decisions through late 2022, directly bearing on the 2023 inherited project status.","ruler_attribution":"The project, promises, decree, and construction decisions are attributed to López Obrador’s government.","limitations":["Some environmental-damage estimates are attributed to experts or observers rather than official measurement."]},{"source_id":"SRC-a56749c2c8afadc2","start_unit":6,"end_unit":8,"fact_summary":"The government acknowledged 300,000 trees felled along section five, while observers estimated substantially more; the project’s budget approached $20 billion, about three times the original estimate. The government reported job creation, while local accounts described fear of reprisal, pressured land concessions, and concerns that construction threatened jungle, homes, and cenotes.","question_ids":["3B.3","3B.7","4B.3","5B.5","5B.6","5B.8","6B.3","6B.8","7B.9","8B.6","8B.7","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The evidence concerns project implementation before and around the beginning of 2023.","ruler_attribution":"Government job and tree figures, public messaging, and project decisions are attributed to López Obrador’s administration; local concerns are independently reported.","limitations":["The article does not resolve the disputed tree count or quantify the net employment effect."]},{"source_id":"SRC-5392914320e996fa","start_unit":7,"end_unit":9,"fact_summary":"Mexico’s electoral authority warned that the proposed Plan B reforms could weaken INE autonomy, territorial and professional capacity, electoral training, gender-equality and affirmative-action structures, fiscal oversight, data protection, local electoral bodies, and the reliability of the electoral register; INE officials instructed legal challenges against the reform.","question_ids":["4B.1","4B.2","4B.4","4B.6","4B.7","4B.9","4B.10","7B.6","7B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The INE statement was issued January 25, 2023, directly within the target period.","ruler_attribution":"The reforms were associated with López Obrador’s governing coalition and legislative agenda; the document records the INE’s institutional assessment rather than a judicial final ruling.","limitations":["The source describes anticipated consequences and legal objections; it does not establish that every warned consequence occurred."]},{"source_id":"SRC-c5ac49244b8ba9af","start_unit":1,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"Banxico’s institutional account states that constitutional autonomy since 1994 gives the bank a primary price-stability mandate, a five-member fixed-term governing board, restrictions on removal, and transparency and accountability mechanisms; it attributes the design to protecting monetary policy from short-term political and fiscal pressures.","question_ids":["5B.2","5B.3","5B.7","8B.2","8B.4","8B.5","8B.6"],"polarity":"context","period_fit":"The source describes the standing institutional framework governing Banxico during 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The source does not attribute the autonomy framework to López Obrador; it supplies institutional context for assessing presidential pressure and constraints.","limitations":["It is an official institutional history and does not independently assess López Obrador’s conduct."]},{"source_id":"SRC-ec1844926b4c52f5","start_unit":20,"end_unit":24,"fact_summary":"CPJ reported that Mexico had 28 unsolved journalist murders during the prior decade, ranked sixth on its 2022 Global Impunity Index, recorded at least 13 journalist killings in the first nine months of 2022, and that López Obrador regularly launched verbal attacks on the media while reporters faced threats; arrests had not generally produced convictions.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.3","3B.4","3B.8","3B.10","4B.3","4B.6","6B.10","7B.2","7B.7","7B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The source covers 2012–August 2022 and is a pre-2023 baseline relevant to the 2023 period; it does not provide 2023 murder statistics.","ruler_attribution":"CPJ directly attributes recurring verbal media attacks to López Obrador and evaluates the authorities’ accountability record.","limitations":["The source does not establish that López Obrador ordered or personally caused any journalist killing."]},{"source_id":"SRC-3b458b07be7515cb","start_unit":1,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"CONEVAL’s process evaluation found that Sembrando Vida had clear beneficiary-selection rules, updated its registry monthly, used District CACs to share solutions, and provided technical accompaniment; it also found supply shortages, inadequate plants, insufficient distribution infrastructure, banking bottlenecks, limited local-operational participation in planning, and missing or insufficient outcome indicators.","question_ids":["5B.6","5B.7","5B.8","5B.9","6B.2","6B.3","6B.4","6B.5","6B.7","6B.9","8B.2","8B.3","8B.5","8B.6","8B.7","8B.8"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The evaluation was published in 2022 and assesses the program after three years of implementation, providing operational evidence entering 2023.","ruler_attribution":"Sembrando Vida is identified as a federal priority program implemented by the López Obrador administration.","limitations":["The evaluation is qualitative and does not provide a complete 2023 outcome assessment."]},{"source_id":"SRC-47446200367ad461","start_unit":2,"end_unit":6,"fact_summary":"México Evalúa reported persistent under-execution of approved health-investment budgets from 2019 through 2022, including a 62% delay by the third quarter of 2022; it found that spending on the Maya Train and defense projects exceeded period allocations while health infrastructure investment lagged, and that the number of health units declined, especially small clinics serving poorer communities.","question_ids":["5B.1","5B.6","5B.7","5B.9","5B.10","6B.2","6B.3","6B.4","6B.5","6B.6","6B.10","8B.2","8B.3","8B.6","8B.7","8B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The report was published December 2022 and evaluates the administration’s health-investment record through the third quarter of 2022, relevant to the 2023 starting position.","ruler_attribution":"Budget priorities and execution patterns are attributed to the federal government under López Obrador.","limitations":["The report is an external analysis and includes projections for year-end 2022."]},{"source_id":"SRC-a131d59a4f70fb1b","start_unit":1,"end_unit":7,"fact_summary":"The CNDH monitoring portal recorded low compliance ratings for international recommendations concerning women and children with disabilities, accessible health and emergency services, national accessibility planning, Indigenous consultation and land rights, protection against forced displacement, discrimination, justice access, journalist investigations, and protection mechanisms for defenders and journalists.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.4","3B.7","3B.8","3B.9","3B.10","4B.3","4B.7","5B.8","6B.2","6B.3","6B.5","6B.6","6B.8","6B.9","6B.10","7B.2","7B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The portal reports compliance status for recommendations relevant to Mexico’s 2023 human-rights context, though the recommendations span earlier reporting periods.","ruler_attribution":"The ratings concern the Mexican state and federal implementation; they do not isolate López Obrador’s personal decisions in every area.","limitations":["The page aggregates recommendations and compliance ratings without a full explanation of each rating’s measurement date or methodology."]},{"source_id":"SRC-31991de01aa8a267","start_unit":8,"end_unit":13,"fact_summary":"CSIS reported that López Obrador’s administration transferred major civilian functions to the armed forces, including infrastructure, tourism, customs, migration, public health, and banking; it described limited civilian supervision, national-security exemptions from scrutiny, weakened procurement transparency, politicization toward Morena, and military noncooperation in the Ayotzinapa disappearance case.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.5","3B.6","3B.9","3B.10","4B.2","4B.4","4B.5","4B.9","4B.10","5B.5","5B.6","7B.6","7B.7","7B.9","7B.10","8B.2","8B.3","8B.4","8B.5","8B.6","8B.8","8B.9","8B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Published September 2023, the analysis directly assesses the administration’s trajectory during the target year.","ruler_attribution":"The expansion and political direction of militarization are explicitly attributed to López Obrador and his administration.","limitations":["The article is expert commentary and presents some causal and predictive judgments rather than a comprehensive official audit."]},{"source_id":"SRC-98f9fa4ab5689d94","start_unit":6,"end_unit":11,"fact_summary":"CONEVAL’s 2016–2022 poverty-and-gender indicators showed persistent gendered inequality: women worked fewer paid hours and more unpaid domestic hours, faced wider labor-participation and wage gaps in poverty, lower social-security coverage, greater food insecurity and educational disadvantage in older age, and lower direct income stability; older-person transfer coverage expanded, but transfers declined for other groups, especially poor women.","question_ids":["5B.8","5B.10","6B.2","6B.3","6B.5","6B.8","6B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The series ends in 2022 and provides the closest available outcome baseline entering 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The indicators describe national conditions during López Obrador’s administration but do not attribute each outcome solely to presidential policy.","limitations":["The source is descriptive and does not establish causal attribution to specific federal programs."]},{"source_id":"SRC-986a60dd23d33a32","start_unit":3,"end_unit":6,"fact_summary":"Mexico’s 2023 UN statement presented a program centered on poverty reduction, social programs, minimum-wage increases, environmental sustainability, Escazú implementation, climate adaptation, nuclear disarmament and nonproliferation, peaceful dispute resolution, and support for dialogue in Colombia and Venezuela; it condemned Russia’s invasion of Ukraine and reaffirmed treaty-based multilateralism.","question_ids":["1B.1","1B.2","1B.4","1B.5","1B.8","1B.10","2B.1","2B.3","2B.7","2B.10","5B.1","5B.8","6B.1","6B.10","8B.1","8B.2","8B.9"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The statement was delivered September 23, 2023, directly within the target period.","ruler_attribution":"The statement was delivered on behalf of Mexico and explicitly conveyed President López Obrador’s government’s positions.","limitations":["The statement establishes declared commitments, not independent evidence of implementation or outcomes."]},{"source_id":"SRC-986a60dd23d33a32","start_unit":8,"end_unit":10,"fact_summary":"Mexico’s UN statement declared a feminist foreign policy, support for gender equality and sexual diversity, humanized migration, multilateral development, and urgent action on climate and inequality, while acknowledging that international commitments require concrete results.","question_ids":["3B.7","4B.7","5B.8","6B.1","6B.3","6B.8","6B.10","8B.1","8B.2","8B.7"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The statement was delivered in September 2023.","ruler_attribution":"These were official positions of Mexico’s government under López Obrador, delivered by the foreign secretary.","limitations":["The document is programmatic and diplomatic; it does not verify domestic execution."]}],"documents_with_no_material_fact":[],"batch_limitations":["The supplied corpus is uneven in date: several sources describe 2022 or earlier conditions used as the baseline for 2023, while other sources directly address 2023.","The sources contain advocacy, institutional, journalistic, and analytical perspectives; facts are reported with attribution and without converting claims into scores."]}
